title: How would you design idempotency for a payment API?
description: Idempotency ensures that calling a payment API multiple times has the same effect as calling it once — critical for retries and network glitches.

data.text: Payments are one domain where idempotency is non-negotiable. Networks glitch, clients retry, and users double-click. If a charge call is processed twice, the customer is charged twice. Idempotency means that submitting the same payment request multiple times produces the same result — one charge — without side effects.

The industry standard is the Idempotency-Key pattern, popularized by Stripe. The client generates a unique key for each logical payment attempt and sends it with the request. The server stores the result of the first execution and returns the stored result for any subsequent request with the same key.

items: Client generates a UUID v4 idempotency key before sending the payment request.
Server checks whether that key already exists in the idempotency records table.
If it exists and the original request completed, return the stored result immediately.
If it exists but the original request is still processing, return 409 Conflict or a polling endpoint.
If it does not exist, process the payment, store the key with the result, and return the result.

data.text: The idempotency record must be written before any external charge is attempted. This prevents a window where a retry could create a duplicate charge. The record captures the request parameters, the result, and a timestamp for expiry cleanup.

data.title: SQL Server: Idempotency records table
data.code:
CREATE TABLE PaymentIdempotency (
    IdempotencyKey CHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    PaymentId CHAR(36) NULL,
    Status        NVARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    RequestBody   NVARCHAR(MAX) NOT NULL,
    ResponseBody  NVARCHAR(MAX) NULL,
    CreatedAt     DATETIME2 NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSUTCDATETIME(),
    ExpiresAt     DATETIME2 NOT NULL
);

CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_PaymentIdempotency_ExpiresAt
ON PaymentIdempotency (ExpiresAt);

data.title: Minimal API endpoint with idempotency guard

items: Key lifetime: expire records after a reasonable window (24-72 hours) to keep the table small.
Atomicity: write the idempotency record in the same transaction scope as any internal ledger entries to prevent orphan states.
Concurrency: use the idempotency key as the primary key so the database enforces uniqueness naturally.
Client responsibility: the client must generate a fresh key for each new logical payment, not reuse old keys.

data.title: Never charge first and record later
data.text: Always write the idempotency record before calling the payment processor. If the charge succeeds but the record write fails, you have no way to detect and prevent a duplicate on retry.

items: What happens if two requests arrive with the same key simultaneously? (Answer: database primary-key constraint + transaction isolation handles it.)
How do you handle key expiry without losing traceability? (Answer: move completed records to an archive table before deleting.)
Should the idempotency check happen before authentication or after? (Answer: authenticate first to avoid leaking payment state to unauthenticated callers.)

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Generate the idempotency key on the client and pass it in every request header.
Write the idempotency record before any external charge to close the duplicate window.
Use the key as the primary key so the database enforces uniqueness automatically.
Return the stored response for duplicate keys — do not re-process.
data.takeaway: Idempotency is about writing the marker before taking the action, not after.
